system.name: SwiftSage
system.one_liner: Agent framework pairing a small LM fine-tuned on oracle trajectories (fast) with an LLM planner called only when needed (slow), for ScienceWorld tasks.

content.variant_note: four boxed columns (SayCan, ReAct, Reflexion, SwiftSage) built from the same prompt cards, LLM box and action, with highlights marking what each design changes
content.argues: SayCan, ReAct and Reflexion call an LLM at every timestep; SwiftSage runs a small fine-tuned LM and calls the LLM only when needed for subgoals and grounding.
content.subject: Prompting designs of four LLM agents on the task 'boil tin', each as a stack of prompt cards feeding LLM boxes and an action.

lessons.what_to_learn: Compare agent or prompting designs by drawing each as the same top-down stack of prompt cards, LLM box and output, then colour only the span or box that differs; header tabs say how often each block runs, which shows the cost difference without numbers.
lessons.suits: Comparisons of prompting or agent designs where the difference lies in what enters the prompt and how often the LLM is called.

evidence: SAYCAN [1], REACT [41] and REFLEXION [30] require a new inference with LLMs for each time step
Figure 1: Comparing methods of prompting LLMs to build agents for interactive tasks.

summary: SwiftSage is an agent framework inspired by fast and slow thinking: a small encoder-decoder LM trained on oracle trajectories acts by default, and an LLM plans subgoals and grounds them only when needed. Figure 1 compares prompting designs in four framed columns. SayCan, ReAct and Reflexion each stack grey Demo, Task and Action history cards, send them to an orange LLM box at every timestep and output one action; yellow highlights mark what each adds (reranking, think steps, reflection). The purple SwiftSage column adds the Small LM, an 'Only when needed' block with cyan prompts, two LLM calls and an action buffer.
summary_zh: SwiftSage让小模型快速行动、大模型仅在需要时规划子目标。图1用四列对比SayCan、ReAct、Reflexion和SwiftSage：同样的提示卡片栈接橙色LLM框，高亮标出差异，前三者每步都调用LLM。
notes: Highlight colours have no legend; their meanings (yellow = what a baseline adds, cyan = SwiftSage-specific) are read from the figure and the paper text. The SVG carries many bitmaps (LLM boxes, arrows, icons) from PowerPoint shapes, so no data pictures are recorded. The house icon is read as the environment; the figure does not name it.
